h1: ChomTrang — a budget stay opposite Trang railway station you can reach by stepping off the train and crossing the road
intro: If you arrive in Trang on an early train and want a cheap stay you can reach by just crossing the road, no taxi needed, ChomTrang is a small property sitting directly opposite Trang railway station, and many reviews call it better value than the price suggests. It is a 2-star budget hotel of 12 rooms that are clean and bigger than expected, with city-view balconies and included breakfast, within walking distance of the clock tower and night markets. From approx. ฿550/night, scoring 8.4 — what it sells is an in-town location and cleanliness, not big-hotel facilities.

body.html: The thing that makes people choose ChomTrang before anything else is its location directly opposite Trang railway station — step off the train, cross the road, and you are there, no dragging luggage far or calling a ride in the early morning. The hotel sits on Sathani (Station) Road in the city center, surrounded by restaurants, cafes, banks and travel agents. For travellers who come to Trang for morning dim sum, market walks, or using the city as a base before island boat trips, this kind of location works better than a beachfront stay further out.

The property has 12 rooms, split into Deluxe Double and Deluxe Twin. The thing reviews mention most is rooms that are clean and bigger than expected for this price bracket — comfortable beds, good-quality towels, quiet and cold air conditioning, and several rooms with a balcony looking over the town, plus a flat-screen TV, fridge and work desk. The decor is simple and minimalist, well maintained, and feels more like staying in a private apartment than a hotel.
"Stepped off the train and crossed the road, that was it. The room was clean, bigger than I expected, and the A/C was really quiet. Excellent value for a solo traveller."

Another point that earns praise is friendly, helpful staff — many reviews say the owner arranges transfers, advises on onward travel, and helps book island tours. The included breakfast comes with cooked items, toast, tea and coffee, orange juice, cake and fruit, which is generous for a stay at this price. The overall feel is quiet, suiting travellers who just want a proper rest after a day on the move.

Things to know before booking. First, the front desk is not staffed around the clock — sometimes you need to call the local number posted to have someone come and let you in or check you in, so give notice if you arrive outside normal hours. Second, staff speak limited English and some international guests found communication a little tricky. Third, the building has no lift and in-room amenities are fairly basic — some rooms lack shampoo or a kettle, so packing your own toiletries is the safer bet.

Rates start from about ฿550/night for a Deluxe in the low season, rising to roughly ฿650–฿850 in high season or on long weekends. The overall score sits at 8.4 from Trip.com and Agoda reviews, with 4.1/5 on Tripadvisor (ranked #8 of 36 B&Bs in Trang) — figures that reflect a small property scoring well in the budget tier, its strengths being cleanliness, room size and the in-town location.

In short, ChomTrang suits budget travellers who want a central Trang stay focused on a clean, spacious room and a walkable location — especially anyone arriving by train, since you cross the road from the station and you are there. But if you need full facilities like a pool, gym or a staffed 24-hour front desk, this kind of small property may not fit → consider a higher-tier city hotel such as Thumrin Thana instead.

A tip drawn from the reviews: ask for an upper-floor room with a city-view balcony, the angle that makes a stay here most worthwhile. And if you arrive late or outside normal hours, message or call the hotel in advance via LINE or phone, since the front desk is not always staffed — that way you will not be left waiting at the door.

honestSummary: ChomTrang is a budget central-Trang stay that stands out for its location opposite the railway station, cleanliness and room size. Its 12 rooms are well kept with city-view balconies, starting at a few hundred baht. But you have to accept that the front desk is not always staffed, amenities are basic, and there are no big-hotel facilities.

faq.q: Where is ChomTrang and how do I get there?
faq.a: It is at 27 Sathani (Station) Road in central Trang, directly opposite Trang railway station — step off the train, cross the road and you are there. About a 10-minute walk to Trang Clock Tower, Wat Tantayapirom and the night market, and roughly 15 minutes by car from Trang Airport (TST).

faq.q: How much is ChomTrang and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from about ฿550/night for a Deluxe Double. Deluxe Twin is around ฿600 and a room with breakfast about ฿700, while high season nudges up to roughly ฿850. Prices vary by date — always compare a few platforms before booking.

It suits budget travellers who want a central Trang stay, especially anyone arriving by train. You cross the road from the station, the rooms are clean and spacious, and you can walk to markets and restaurants. Not ideal if you want a pool or big-hotel facilities.

faq.q: Does ChomTrang have breakfast, and is it good?
faq.a: Yes, breakfast is included in some rates, with cooked items, toast, tea and coffee, orange juice, cake and fruit — generous for the price. On some days it can be late or simpler than usual; if you want a proper meal, try Trang's famous dim sum spots nearby as well.

faq.q: What should I watch out for at check-in?
faq.a: The front desk is not staffed around the clock — sometimes you need to call the local number posted to have someone let you in. If you arrive late or outside normal hours, message or call via LINE in advance so you are not left waiting at the door.

faq.q: Is it easy to reach Trang's islands from ChomTrang?
faq.a: Yes — it is central and next to the railway station, and staff can help arrange transport and boat tours to Koh Kradan, Koh Mook, Koh Ngai and the Emerald Cave. Most depart from Pak Meng or Kuan Tung Ku piers, about a 40–50 minute drive from the city before the boat.
